title: Isomorphic Strings
statement: Two strings are isomorphic when the characters of the first can be replaced to give the second, with every occurrence of a character replaced the same way, and no two different characters mapping to the same one. A character may map to itself.
constraints: the strings are the same length
the mapping must be one-to-one in BOTH directions
hints: One dictionary from s-characters to t-characters is the obvious start, and it is not enough on its own.
Consider "ab" and "aa". A single forward map happily sends a to a and b to a, but that is two characters collapsing onto one, which is not allowed.
So keep both directions and reject any conflict in either. Alternatively, compare the sequence of first-occurrence positions of each string - two strings are isomorphic exactly when those match.
complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space for a fixed alphabet

cases.name: forward map alone would wrongly accept
reverse map alone would wrongly accept
